# Sudipta Deb (debkosh.com)

Personal site of Sudipta Deb, who leads Ulaa — a Chromium-based enterprise
browser — and its built-in SASE stack, and builds developer tools on the
side. The blog is long-form writing on enterprise browser security,
proxies, and enforcement mechanics: how things actually work and what the
tradeoffs really cost.

## Main pages

- [Home](https://debkosh.com/)
- [Blog](https://debkosh.com/blogs)
- [Lab (projects)](https://debkosh.com/labs)
- [RSS feed](https://debkosh.com/rss.xml)

## Projects

- [memd](https://github.com/sudiptadeb/memd): file-first memory for AI
  agents — markdown files you own and version. Also at
  https://memd.debkosh.com
- [linfer](https://github.com/sudiptadeb/linfer): the best local LLM
  inference setup for your machine; picks llama.cpp or MLX, installs it,
  fetches and sizes the model, serves one OpenAI-compatible URL.
- [linfer-bench](https://github.com/sudiptadeb/linfer-bench): benchmarks
  OpenAI-compatible endpoints the way agents use them — speed, tool-calling
  accuracy, needle retrieval — and compares tagged runs.
- [amarit](https://github.com/sudiptadeb/amarit): keep it alive, keep it
  current — self-update for Go programs from a release manifest, with
  rollback, plus a keep-alive daemon under launchd, systemd or nothing.
- [termulaa](https://github.com/sudiptadeb/termulaa): terminal and coding
  agents in a browser tab, with sessions that survive the tab closing.
- [keysat](https://github.com/sudiptadeb/keysat): local-first keystroke
  and activity tracking for macOS; never leaves the machine.
- [sackup](https://github.com/sudiptadeb/sackup): phone backup to a USB
  drive — offline, resumable, verified.
